page.text:
While subgroups isolate the internal substructures of a group, *quotient
groups* perform the dual geometric task: collapsing indistinguishable
elements to reveal large-scale structure.

However, forming a quotient group requires more than an arbitrary
subgroup: coset multiplication $(gH)(hH) = (gh)H$ is well-defined if and
only if the subgroup is *normal* ($gHg^{-1} = H$ for all $g$). Group
actions provide the external, dynamical counterpart to this internal
architecture: an abstract group is realized as a group of transformations
acting on a geometric set. The concepts of kernel, normal subgroup,
orbit, and stabilizer interweave these perspectives into a unified theory
of mathematical symmetry.
